headline: BEANS HOLD $12.99; CRUDE AT $100, WEEK AHEAD
lead: Soybeans closed Friday at $12.99 after shedding 24 cents on the WASDE print, and that level is now the line every unpriced bushel is measured against. Crude held just under $100 as oil traders priced a longer Iran conflict, not a resolution.
teaser: Beans stuck at $12.99, crude below $100, and a week that will answer both questions.

one_number.context: USDA cut corn yield 2.3 bu from July on the Aug 12 WASDE. Early harvest reports this week are the first field check against that number.

yesterdays_call.call_line: Called soybeans down toward $12.85 ($12.99 when the call was made). It closed at $12.99.
yesterdays_call.note: Beans held $12.99 all session; the $12.85 target never threatened -- a clean miss on timing.

action: Unpriced new-crop beans: hold above $12.99; a close below $12.85 any day this week is the sale signal, not a reason to watch further.

sections.title: BEANS AND CORN: WASDE HANGOVER
sections.body: - November beans closed Friday at **$12.99**, right where the WASDE drop left them; the bounce that would say 'noise' never came, and the weekend gave nobody a reason to own them.
sections.so_what: Beans need a bid Monday or $12.85 becomes the next test by midweek.

sections.title: CRUDE BELOW $100; IRAN WAR PRICED LONGER
sections.body: - WTI closed Friday at **$99.99**, off 3.1%, as the Iran-Hormuz cycle (a re-escalation that has run since July, with the Strait effectively shut since March per oil traders) shifted from acute-risk to priced-in-for-years framing.
sections.so_what: Crude under $100 is not a buying window for farmers; lock fall diesel now.

sections.title: CATTLE FIRMS; FEEDERS PUSH HIGHER
sections.body:
- Live cattle closed at **$219.62**, up 0.8%, and feeders at $337.88, up 1.6%, with political noise around mCOOL and beef imports adding headline volatility but not changing the processing-constrained fundamental.
- The Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still removes roughly 6,000 head of daily capacity; the cattle are there, the kill slots are not.
sections.so_what: Cattle firm on tight processing, not demand; watch the Douglas reopening pace.

outside_the_pit.title: Oil Industry Models Years-Long Iran War, Not a Cycle
outside_the_pit.body: Producers and refiners are now planning for a structural Iran conflict, not an episode. That reprices crude risk from seasonal to structural and keeps diesel elevated through 2027.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress: corn harvest pace above 10% says early fields are moving; below 5% adds weather and yield uncertainty.
Export Sales: beans under 700K MT keeps the WASDE break in charge; above 900K MT is the first recovery signal.
November beans vs $12.85: a close below it confirms WASDE direction; hold is the only trade above it.

daily_quote.text: Know what you own, and know why you own it.

source_summary: USDA WASDE Aug 12, USDA Crop Progress, CME Friday closes, farmdocdaily.illinois.edu, oilprice.com, beefmagazine.com, feedstuffs.com
